question: Distance of a chord JK from the centre is 7 cm. If diameter of this circle is 50 cm, then what will be length of this chord?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a circle, the **radius**, **distance from center**, and **half-chord length** form a **right-angled triangle**.

Radius (r) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm. Distance (d) = 7 cm.

Using the **Pythagorean triplet** (7, 24, 25):

Half-chord length = 24 cm.

Length of chord **JK** = 2 × 24 = 48 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 50 cm

Distance of chord **JK** from centre (**O**) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2

In ▵**OMJ** (Right-angled), **OJ² = OM² + MJ²** (Pythagoras Theorem)

Chord length **JK** = 2 × **MJ** (Perpendicular from center bisects the chord)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/86d7329b3da31f25dc3ac04003c489f57acd3c903ee6907c5ae688bbee67bd56.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius (r) = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 cm

⇒ In right ▵**OMJ**, **OJ** = 25 cm and **OM** = 7 cm

⇒ **MJ²** = **OJ²** − **OM²**

⇒ **MJ²** = 25² − 7²

⇒ **MJ²** = 625 − 49 = 576

⇒ **MJ** = √576 = 24 cm

⇒ Total length of chord **JK** = 2 × **MJ**

⇒ **JK** = 2 × 24 = 48 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular Bisector Property

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17), are extremely useful for quick circle calculations.

Chord Distance Relation

Chords that are equidistant from the center of a circle are equal in length, and longer chords are closer to the center.</p
